title: THE DOOM OF THE UNGODLY
mv: For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, But the way of the ungodly shall perish.
mvp: “For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, But the way of the ungodly shall perish.” Psalm 1:6 (NKJV)
assignment: Describe the ungodly in five (5) simple ways (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: The first part of Psalm one (verses 1-3) addresses the blessedness of the righteous while the second part (verses 4-6) addresses the end of the wicked. In this lesson, we shall describe the ungodly as well as look into his doom.

The Psalmist describes the ungodly as the reverse of the righteous both in character and condition - “The ungodly are not so, But are like the chaff which the wind drives away” (Psalm 1:4). “The ungodly are not so” means they are led by the counsel of the wicked (Proverbs 16:27), in the way of sinners (Proverbs 4:14-15), to the seat of the scornful (Proverbs 19:28). They have no delight in the law of God nor ever think of it. They bring forth no fruit but grapes of Sodom (Romans 1:29-32).

Secondly, “…But are like the chaff which the wind drives away” means they are of no worth at all in God’s account, no matter how highly they value themselves (Isaiah 17:13-14). They are vain and empty without the knowledge of God (Psalm 10:4, 14:1). They have no substance in them (Nahum 2:10). They are easily driven to and fro by every wind of doctrine and temptation of Satan (Hebrews 13:9; James 1:14-15). They are not steadfast (2 Peter 2:14-15). They neither have root or moisture (Mark 4:5-6). They are destitute of all that is good (Romans 7:18; Proverbs 17:20a). They are sensual, and do not have the Spirit of God (Jude 19).

Psalm 1:5 says, “Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgement, Nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.” On the day of judgement, the ungodly shall be found guilty (Psalm 9:17; Romans 1:18). They shall bow their head in shame and confusion, and all their pleas and excuses shall be overruled as frivolous (Psalm 44:15; Proverbs 3:35). Their future state will be determined by an irreversible sentence (Luke 13:27). “..Nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous” means they will be driven away from the presence of the Lord into everlasting destruction (Job 21:17; Hosea 13:2-3). They shall not stand in the same place with the righteous (Matthew 25:41).

Finally, God is angry with the ungodly (Psalm 7:11). Psalm 1:6 tells us that the way of the ungodly shall perish because the very way they have chosen and resolve to walk naturally tends towards destruction (Proverbs 10:29; Proverbs 14:12). Their way shall perish because all they do is offensive to Him (Psalm 37:20).
The activities of the righteous and the ungodly are wide open unto God. He punishes the ungodly and rewards the righteous (Psalm 1:6; Psalm 7:11).

i: Briefly describe the state of the ungodly.
